svg.text: π / σ / ω = orbital type (ω = lone pair or empty p)
number = ELECTRONS in that component (not atoms)
s = same face at both ends · a = opposite faces (twist)
q, r values are never used — only the class
Why odd: HOMO of one component must meet the LUMO of
the other in phase at every new bond; a LUMO has the
opposite end-symmetry to its own HOMO → exactly one
• allyl cation (3 atoms) = 2 e⁻ → (4q+2); allyl anion = 4 e⁻
• tropone reacts as π6 (the C=O π is not used)
• ketene: the C=C reacts (π2a), not the whole C=C=O
• σ C–H or C–C = 2 e⁻; lone pair ω2; empty p ω0
• [i,j] in sigmatropic names = ATOMS, not electrons
• atoms = electrons only for neutral all-C polyenes
Allowed ≠ happens: the twist (a) must be feasible
• ketene: sp C, no substituent + orthogonal C=O π* → works
• simple alkene crossed: 2 bonding vs 2 antibonding, H clash → no
• [1,7]-H: long chain coils (helix) → works; [1,3]-H: too short → no
